Quarto, R Markdown, Word and PDF output

Source: vignettes/articles/quarto-word-pdf.Rmd
quarto-word-pdf.Rmd
library(niceSMD)
d <- example_table1_data()
tab <- nice_SMD_table1(
  d, "group", c("age", "sex", "smoking"),
  group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"), notes = "short"
)

In a Quarto or R Markdown document

Put the object as the last expression of a chunk:

# inside a .qmd or .Rmd code chunk
tab

niceSMD registers a knit_print method, so tab is rendered as a formatted table (bold variable names, indented levels, footnotes) in HTML, Word, and PDF output. Printing it at the console gives a plain-text version with the same structure. The table below is rendered that way:

Categorical variables: n (%) among nonmissing values. Continuous variables: mean (SD) and median (Q1, Q3). Missing: n (% of group).

SMD = absolute standardized mean difference (Control vs. Treatment); NE = not estimable.

If you assign the result (tab <- nice_SMD_table1(...)) the chunk prints nothing; end the chunk with tab to display it. nice_trial_table1() results render the same way.

Controlling size and fonts

For a different font or size, end the chunk with the flextable instead:

table1_flextable(tab, font_size = 9, font_family = "Arial")

Wide tables (many groups, or trial tables) read better in a smaller font or, in Word, a landscape section.

Further styling with flextable

table1_flextable() returns an ordinary flextable, so any flextable function applies:

ft <- table1_flextable(tab)
ft <- flextable::bg(ft, part = "header", bg = "#EAF0F4")
ft <- flextable::color(ft, part = "header", color = "#243746")
ft

Word files 

# Standalone Word file
save_table1_docx(tab, "Table1.docx", landscape = TRUE, font_size = 9)

# Or write while building the table
nice_SMD_table1(d, "group", "age", group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"),
                docx_path = "Table1.docx")

# Export a flextable you modified yourself
flextable::save_as_docx(`Participant characteristics` = ft, path = "Custom.docx")

save_table1_docx() never overwrites an existing file unless you set overwrite = TRUE. Headers repeat on each page, and a variable’s name stays with its first row.

PDF output

Table rendering to PDF goes through LaTeX. If flextable’s PDF output has font or package problems on your machine, table1_kable() is a lighter alternative that needs only knitr:

table1_kable(tab)                    # chunk ending: renders in the document format
table1_kable(tab, format = "latex")  # force LaTeX
cat(tab$notes, sep = "\n")           # footnotes are printed separately

Extracting numbers 

as.data.frame(tab)[1:3, ]            # the display table
#>          Variable        Control\nN = 30       Treatment\nN = 30
#> 1             age                                               
#> 2       Mean (SD)         147.28 (60.78)          358.55 (61.66)
#> 3 Median (Q1, Q3) 148.00 (99.00, 197.00) 360.00 (311.00, 409.00)
#>          Registry\nN = 30 SMD (Control vs. Treatment)
#> 1                                               3.451
#> 2          570.07 (62.10)                            
#> 3 572.00 (516.00, 621.00)
tab$smd[, c("label", "smd", "status")]  # unrounded SMDs
#>     label        smd status
#> 1     age 3.45103284     ok
#> 2     sex 0.00000000     ok
#> 3 smoking 0.09313035     ok
